Why CoolIn

Why people hand us the job

Most complaints in this trade are not about the equipment. They are about a system sized on a guess, a price that moves once the pipework is halfway up the wall, or a company that answers the phone in June and not in January. We put every detail in writing before you commit, turn up when we say, and stand behind the work afterwards. Here is what that means on the day, and more about how we work .

01 One company accountable, start to finish
We survey it, we specify it, we install it and we come back to service it. One contract, one number to ring, and one company carrying the risk if something needs putting right.

02 Fixed price, written down
Your quote lists the units, the pipe runs, the electrical work and the making good. No day rates, no extras added halfway through.

03 We leave it cleaner than we found it
Dust sheets down, core drilling done wet, and a hoover in the van. When we pull off the drive you should not be able to tell we were ever there.

04 Certified work, and we will prove it
No refrigerant circuit is opened on your system by anyone without current F-Gas certification, and the electrical side is certified under Part P on completion. Ask to see either certificate and you will get it.

05 Everything written down and handed over
Commissioning readings, the manufacturer warranty registered in your name, certificates for the work carried out and a drawing of where the pipework runs. It goes in a pack rather than being promised verbally.

Common questions

The things people ask on the first call

More detail on the domestic and commercial pages, where the questions get more specific.

How long does an installation take?

A single room is usually one day. A three or four room multi split is two days. Commercial projects depend on the number of units and the access, and we give you a day by day plan with the quote.

Does it need servicing every year?

Yes, and the manufacturers require it to keep the warranty running. A service is a filter clean, a coil clean, a gas pressure check and a drain test. Our plans start at £89 per unit and include priority callout.

Which areas do you cover?

Roughly an hour from our base in Manchester, which takes in Greater Manchester, most of Cheshire, Merseyside and southern Lancashire. The full list is further down this page. If you are just outside it, ring us anyway and we will either come to you or point you at someone who can.

What standard is the work held to?

Nobody opens a refrigerant circuit on your system without current F-Gas certification. That is a legal requirement for handling refrigerant rather than a badge, and we will show you the certificate if you want to see it. Electrical work is notifiable under Part P and is certified on completion.

CoolIn holds the contract throughout. We invoice you, our own workmanship is guaranteed for two years on top of the manufacturer warranty, and if something needs putting right you ring us rather than chasing anyone else.

Types of system

Four ways to cool a home, and when each one is right

Almost every home comes down to one of these. The survey decides which, based on your rooms, your ceilings, where the outdoor unit can go, and how much you want to see on the wall.

Wall mounted split

One room, one indoor unit

from £1,850installed

The standard domestic unit and the one most people picture. A slim indoor unit high on the wall, a condenser outside, and two copper pipes plus a drain between them.

Best for
Bedrooms, lounges, home offices, loft conversions, conservatories

Sizes
2.0kW to 7.1kW, covering roughly 12m² to 45m²

Worth knowing
Quiet ranges start around 19 dB(A) indoors, about the same as a whisper. Nearly all current models take app control as standard.

Multi split

Two to five rooms, one outdoor unit

from £3,450installed

Several indoor units share a single condenser, so you get three or four cooled rooms with only one box outside. Every room still sets its own temperature.

Best for
Whole homes, flats with limited outdoor space, anywhere a second condenser would look wrong

Sizes
Outdoor units from 4.0kW to around 10kW

Worth knowing
The outdoor unit caps the total. Four 2.5kW indoor units on a 7.2kW condenser gives 7.2kW shared between them when everything runs at once, not 10kW. We size the condenser for how you actually use the rooms.

Ducted and concealed

Nothing on show but grilles

from £3,500installed

The indoor unit hides in a loft, bulkhead or ceiling void and feeds two or more rooms through short duct runs. All you see in the room is a slim grille.

Best for
New builds, full renovations, period interiors where a wall unit would jar

Sizes
3.5kW upwards, often serving two or three rooms from one unit

Worth knowing
Far easier during building work than afterwards. It can also be paired with a fresh air supply , which wall units cannot do.

Floor standing console

Low level, like a radiator

from £2,150installed

Sits at skirting level under a window or in an alcove. Because it throws warm air out at floor level it is the better choice when the system will do a lot of heating.

Best for
Rooms with no spare wall height, conservatories, under sloped ceilings, replacing a radiator

Sizes
2.5kW to 7.1kW

Worth knowing
Keep furniture clear of the front and top. Blocking it costs you more output than people expect.

Home air conditioning in short

A domestic air conditioning system is an air to air heat pump : it cools a room in summer and heats it in winter from the same unit. A single wall mounted system fitted in one room costs from £1,850 with no VAT to add, takes one day to install, and delivers around 4.5kWh of heat for every 1kWh of electricity it uses.

One room
From £1,850 fitted, 2.5kW, rooms to 15m²

Whole home

VAT
0% on domestic installs until 31 March 2027

Install time
One day for a single room, two for a multi split

Running cost
About 7p to 16p an hour to cool a bedroom

Planning permission
Not usually needed since 29 May 2025

Sizing

Getting the size right matters more than the badge on the front

Undersize it and the room never quite gets there on the hottest day. Oversize it and the unit short cycles, which is noisier, less efficient and harder on the compressor. Here is the starting point we work from, then the survey confirms it.

Typical unit output by room size
| | Room | Floor area | Typical unit

| Study, small bedroom, box room | up to 15 m² | 2.0 to 2.5 kW

| Double bedroom, small lounge | 15 to 22 m² | 3.5 kW

| Large lounge, kitchen diner | 22 to 32 m² | 5.0 kW

| Open plan ground floor | 32 to 45 m² | 6.0 to 7.1 kW

| Anything larger | 45 m² and up | two or more units

What pushes the size up

South or west facing glass, especially bifolds and roof lights

Loft conversions and rooms in the roof, which take heat from above all day

Ceilings over 2.4m, because you are cooling volume rather than floor

Conservatories and garden rooms, which are effectively greenhouses

Kitchens, server cabinets, gym kit, and rooms full of people

Solid brick walls with no insulation

We work out a room by room heat gain rather than guessing from floor area alone. It takes longer at survey and it is the reason systems we fit do not sit running flat out in August.

0% VAT

Domestic installs are zero rated until 31 March 2027

Since May 2023, energy saving materials fitted in homes carry no VAT, and HMRC treats most air conditioning units as air source heat pumps because they heat as well as cool. The relief applies when the same company supplies and installs the system, which is why buying a unit online and paying someone to fit it does not qualify.

From 1 April 2027 the rate is set to return to 5%. Commercial work is charged at the standard rate, although businesses can usually reclaim it and may be able to claim capital allowances on the equipment.

Source: HMRC VAT Notice 708/6 , checked September 2026.

Tax treatment depends on your circumstances. We put the VAT position in writing on your quote, and your accountant should confirm anything you plan to reclaim.

Against the gas boiler

What it costs to heat a room this way instead of firing the boiler

A boiler burns gas to make heat. A heat pump moves heat that is already outside, which is why it can deliver four and a half units of warmth for one unit of electricity. Change the figures below to your own house and your own tariff.

Your room

How we worked that out

The assumptions

Heat pump seasonal efficiency of 4.5, which is normal for a current A+++ wall unit

Gas boiler running at 88% across a season, rather than the number on the badge

The room calling for about 60% of its peak heat loss on average

Your tariffs, as typed in above

What it does not tell you

It only heats rooms with an indoor unit, so it supplements a boiler rather than replacing one

Output drops below about 5°C outside, when the boiler still has the edge

It gives you no hot water

Cooling in summer is the other half of what you are buying, and the boiler cannot do that at any price

There is a fuller comparison, including where the boiler still wins, in air conditioning against a gas boiler . Every figure here is an estimate from a simple model, not a guarantee. Real bills move with the weather, the thermostat and how well the room holds heat. We will talk through your actual numbers at the survey.

Running costs and efficiency

What it costs to run, and what the numbers on the label mean

Air conditioning does not make cold, it moves heat. That is why a unit drawing 600W of electricity can shift 2,500W of heat, and why it is usually cheaper to heat a room this way than with anything else electric.

Cooling a bedroom

7p to 16pper hour

A 2.5kW unit pulling roughly 0.3kW once the room is down to temperature, up to about 0.65kW while it is working hard. Most nights it spends far more time ticking over than flat out.

Heating that same room

5.6pper kWh of heat

With a seasonal heating efficiency of about 4.5, one unit of electricity gives you roughly four and a half units of heat. Gas in an 88% efficient boiler works out around 7.4p for the same heat.

Against a plug in heater

4x cheaperfor the same warmth

A 2kW fan heater or oil filled radiator gives you exactly 2kW of heat for 2kW of electricity. The heat pump in the same room gives you four times that for the same meter reading.

Figures assume 25p per kWh for electricity and 6.5p per kWh for gas. Swap in your own tariff and the ratios hold, even if the pennies move. We break the sums down further in what air conditioning actually costs to run .

The label, decoded

SEER
Seasonal Energy Efficiency Ratio, for cooling. Units of cooling per unit of electricity across a whole season. Anything from 8.5 up is very good, 6.5 is entry level.

SCOP
The same idea for heating. A SCOP of 4.5 means four and a half units of heat per unit of electricity, averaged over a heating season rather than on a perfect day.

A+ to A+++
The energy class, set from SEER and SCOP. Models are often rated differently for cooling and heating, so check both figures rather than the letter on the box.

Inverter
The compressor varies its speed instead of switching on and off. It holds temperature steadier, runs quieter and uses noticeably less electricity than older fixed speed kit.

R32
The refrigerant in nearly all current units. It has roughly a third of the global warming potential of the R410A it replaced, and the systems need less of it to do the same work.

dB(A)
Noise. Indoor units start around 19 dB(A) on low, quieter than a library. Outdoor units sit in the high 40s to low 50s, which is the figure that matters for neighbours and for planning.

Using it for heating

The things a salesman will not tell you before you buy

Your air conditioning is an air to air heat pump, and in heating mode it behaves differently to a boiler. None of the below is a fault. Knowing it up front is the difference between a customer who is happy in February and one who is not.

01
It heats air, not water

The air to water heat pumps in the news feed radiators and hot water cylinders. Yours moves heat straight into the room through the indoor unit. It will not give you hot taps, and it will not replace your boiler unless every room has a unit.

02
Output falls as it gets colder

There is less heat in the outside air at 2°C than at 10°C, so the system works harder for the same result. Below about 5°C expect longer warm up times, and on the coldest handful of days a second heat source earns its keep.

03
It will blow cool air at you sometimes

Frost builds on the outdoor coil in cold damp weather. Every so often the system reverses for a few minutes to melt it, and the indoor unit goes cool while that happens. It is the defrost cycle, it is normal, and there is no way to switch it off.

04
The outdoor unit drips in winter

Melted frost has to go somewhere. We fit a drain kit and run it to a suitable outlet, but in a hard frost that drain can freeze and water can spill onto the ground below. Where that would be a slip hazard, we can fit heated trace tape at extra cost. It is worth deciding at survey rather than in January.

05
Heat rises, so tall rooms are slow

In a vaulted lounge or a warehouse, the warm air collects above your head while the floor stays cool. That is physics rather than the equipment. Destratification fans push it back down and cut the running time, and we will say so if your room needs one.

06
Guessing the size is normal in this trade

Plenty of quotes are sized on a rule of thumb because a full heat loss calculation costs money and takes time. We do a room by room calculation as part of the survey and show you the working, because it is the single biggest reason a system disappoints in use.

We install home air conditioning right across the North West, including Manchester , Liverpool , Stockport , Bolton , Warrington and Chester . See every town we cover .

Common questions

The things homeowners ask on the first call

How much does air conditioning cost to run?

A modern 2.5kW unit cooling a bedroom costs roughly 20p to 30p an hour at current rates. In heating mode it is usually cheaper per unit of heat than gas, because the system moves heat rather than burning fuel. We put the figures for your specific rooms in the quote.

Do I need planning permission?

For most houses in England, no. The permitted development rules were widened on 29 May 2025 and now cover systems that cool as well as heat. In outline, the outdoor unit can be up to 1.5 cubic metres, detached houses can have two units and everything else one, the old one metre boundary rule has gone, and the installation has to meet the MCS 020 noise standard of 42 dB(A) at the nearest neighbouring habitable room window.

There are limits. It cannot go on a pitched roof, it cannot sit on a wall above ground floor level where that wall faces a highway, and the system must not be for cooling only. Flats are tighter, conservation areas restrict where the unit can sit, and listed buildings and scheduled monuments have no permitted development rights at all.

We check every one of those at survey and tell you before you commit. Where an application is needed, we prepare it. The full rules are set out in our guide to planning permission for air conditioning .

Source: Planning Portal, air source heat pumps , checked September 2026.

How much mess is involved?

One core hole per indoor unit, drilled wet so the dust goes into a bucket rather than your carpet. Everything is sheeted, the pipework is boxed in neatly, and we hoover before we leave.

Is there really no VAT on domestic air conditioning?

Yes, and it is an HMRC rule rather than a discount from us. Energy saving materials installed in homes are zero rated from 1 May 2023 until 31 March 2027, and HMRC's position is that most air conditioning units count as air source heat pumps because they heat as well as cool.

The catch is that the same business has to supply and install it. Buy a unit online and pay someone to fit it and the relief is lost. From April 2027 the rate is expected to go back to 5%. Commercial work is charged at the standard rate.

Source: HMRC VAT Notice 708/6 , checked September 2026.

Will it actually heat the house in winter?

It will heat the rooms that have units in them, quickly and cheaply, down to around 5°C outside. Below that it takes longer to reach temperature and on the coldest few days of the year you will probably want your existing heating as well.

It will not give you hot water, and it only warms the rooms where there is an indoor unit. Anyone telling you a couple of wall units will replace a boiler is overselling it.

How noisy is it, inside and out?

Indoor units on their lowest fan speed run from about 19 dB(A), which is quieter than a library and well under a fridge. On full boost they reach the high 30s or low 40s, which you notice but can talk over.

Outdoor units sit between the high 40s and low 50s at one metre. That is the figure that matters for neighbours, and the planning noise standard is measured at their window rather than at the unit, so distance, fences and positioning all count in your favour.

Where can the outdoor unit go?

On a wall, on the ground on feet, on a flat roof, or on brackets in a lightwell. What it needs is free air: roughly 300mm of clear space behind it and a metre or so in front, nothing boxed in, and somewhere the condensate can drain away.

It also needs to be reachable for servicing, and ideally not directly under a bedroom window, yours or a neighbour's. Long pipe runs from the unit to the rooms are possible but they add cost, so the shortest sensible route usually wins.

What size unit do I need?

As a rough guide, 2.5kW suits a room up to 15m², 3.5kW up to 22m² and 5kW up to 32m². Our size calculator will get you closer using the height, aspect and use of the room.

Those figures move a long way with south facing glass, loft conversions, high ceilings or a kitchen full of appliances. The survey works it out properly rather than rounding up and hoping, which is where oversized, short cycling systems come from.

Does it need its own electrical circuit?

Usually yes. A single wall unit normally runs on a dedicated circuit from the consumer unit through an isolator next to the outdoor unit. Multi splits and larger systems need a bigger circuit again.

That work is notifiable under Part P of the building regulations. It is arranged as part of the job and the certificate goes in your handover pack, so there is no separate electrician for you to find or pay separately.

Can you fit air conditioning in a flat?

Often, but there are two extra hurdles. Your lease usually requires the freeholder's or management company's consent to fix anything to the outside of the building, and the permitted development limits for flats are tighter than for houses.

Where a wall mounted condenser is a non starter, the options are a balcony mounted unit, a shared plant position agreed with the building manager, or a self contained system with no outdoor unit at all. We will tell you at survey which of those applies.

CoolIn / For your business

Who we work for

Every trade has its own problem to solve

A server room and a hair salon both need cooling, and almost nothing about the two jobs is the same. The survey starts with how the space is used, not with a catalogue.

Offices

Even temperatures across a floor plate that has a cold north side and a south facing glass wall. Cassettes zoned so nobody fights over a thermostat, and enough capacity for the meeting room that fills up at two o'clock.

Cassettes, ducted, VRF with zone control

Retail and salons

A shop floor that stays comfortable with the door propped open all day, and units positioned so nobody sits directly under the throw. Colour matched grilles where the ceiling is part of the fit out.

Cassettes and slim ducted, fitted overnight

Restaurants, bars and kitchens

Extract over the line, fresh air make up to replace what the canopy pulls out, and separate cooling for the dining room so the customer side never feels the kitchen. Sized for a full house on a hot Saturday.

Extract, make up air, dedicated front of house

Gyms and studios

Thirty people generating heat in a room with no windows. High air change rates, units placed away from where people lie down, and filtration that copes with the dust a busy floor throws up.

High capacity ducted, ventilation, filtration

Server and comms rooms

Kit that runs at a steady load every hour of the year and fails expensively if it gets hot. Close control cooling with tight temperature and humidity bands, and usually a second system so one can fail without taking the room with it.

Close control, N+1 redundancy, remote alarms

Industrial and warehouse

Big volumes, high ceilings and heat that collects out of reach. Destratification to bring it back down, spot cooling over workstations rather than trying to condition the whole shed, and plant that survives a dusty environment.

Spot cooling, destratification, heavy duty units

Types of system

Six system types, and the buildings each one suits

Most commercial jobs use one of these, or two of them together. The survey starts with your heat load and your ceiling voids rather than with a product list.

Ceiling cassette

Recessed, blows four ways

from £2,450installed

The unit sits up in the ceiling with only a flat grille on show, pushing air out in four directions so a wide room cools evenly rather than from one end.

Best for
Offices, shops, salons, restaurants, and homes with a suspended ceiling

Sizes
3.5kW to 14kW, in 600mm and 900mm cassette formats

Worth knowing
You need roughly 250mm to 350mm of clear void above the ceiling. We check that at survey before anything is quoted.

Ducted and concealed

Nothing on show but grilles

from £3,500installed

The indoor unit hides in a loft, bulkhead or ceiling void and feeds two or more rooms through short duct runs. All you see in the room is a slim grille.

Best for
New builds, full renovations, period interiors where a wall unit would jar

Sizes
3.5kW upwards, often serving two or three rooms from one unit

Worth knowing
Far easier during building work than afterwards. It can also be paired with a fresh air supply, which wall units cannot do.

VRF and VRV

Whole building, mixed unit types

priced per project

One or more large outdoor units feed a whole building through a shared pipe network, with cassettes, wall units and ducted units mixed on the same system. Heat recovery models can heat a north facing office while cooling a server room, moving the heat between them.

Best for
Offices, hotels, retail, multi floor buildings, anything past about eight indoor units

Sizes
From around 12kW to well over 100kW on a single system

Worth knowing
These need a proper design, not a rule of thumb. You get pipework drawings, a heat load, and full operating and maintenance documentation at handover.

Wall mounted split

One room, one indoor unit

from £1,850installed

The standard domestic unit and the one most people picture. A slim indoor unit high on the wall, a condenser outside, and two copper pipes plus a drain between them.

Best for
Bedrooms, lounges, home offices, loft conversions, conservatories

Sizes
2.0kW to 7.1kW, covering roughly 12m² to 45m²

Worth knowing
Quiet ranges start around 19 dB(A) indoors, about the same as a whisper. Nearly all current models take app control as standard.

Close control

Server rooms and comms cabinets

from £9,000installed

Purpose built cooling for rooms where the load never drops and a warm weekend costs real money. Tighter temperature and humidity control than comfort cooling, built to run every hour of the year.

Best for
Server rooms, comms cabinets, labs, anywhere kit matters more than people

Sizes
3.5kW upwards, usually specified in pairs

Worth knowing
Nearly always installed as two systems so one can fail without taking the room down, with remote alarms and four service visits a year rather than one.

Ventilation and heat recovery

Fresh air, extract and make up

from £5,200installed

Cooling recirculates the air already in the room. Ventilation brings new air in and takes stale air out, which is what a packed office, a kitchen canopy or a treatment room actually needs alongside it.

Best for
Kitchens, gyms, salons, meeting rooms, anywhere the air goes stale before it goes warm

Types
Air handling units, heat recovery ventilation, kitchen extract and make up air

Worth knowing
Heat recovery units pull warmth out of the air leaving the building and put it into the air coming in, so you are not paying to heat the street.

Talk it through

Prices per indoor unit. Multiple units on one site are cheaper per unit, and server rooms normally need four visits a year rather than one or two. What each visit covers is set out in full on the servicing page .

F-Gas leak checks

Systems are measured by how much refrigerant they hold, converted into tonnes of CO2 equivalent. Once a system reaches 5 tonnes, the operator has to arrange leak checks by a qualified engineer and keep records.

| | System contains | Leak check

| Under 5 tonnes CO2e | No legal requirement

| 5 to 50 tonnes CO2e | At least every 12 months

| 50 to 500 tonnes CO2e | At least every 6 months

| 500 tonnes CO2e and over | At least every 3 months

In plain terms, with R32 that 5 tonne line sits at roughly 7.4kg of refrigerant. A home split holds one to two kilos, so no checks are due. A commercial VRF usually sits well over the line, and hermetically sealed units under 10 tonnes are exempt either way. We work it out for your system and tell you where you stand.

TM44 inspections for businesses

If you own or manage a building with air conditioning over 12kW of effective rated output, the law requires an inspection by an accredited energy assessor at least every five years, with the first within five years of the system going into service.

That threshold is lower than people assume. Four 3.5kW cassettes in an office already cross it. The report goes on the register, and the duty sits with the building owner or the person controlling the system, not with whoever fitted it.

We flag systems that are over the threshold during servicing so a renewal date never creeps up on you.

How warranties actually work

Manufacturer warranties are parts only and run from five to ten years depending on the brand and on the installer's accreditation level with them. Labour is separate, and comes from the installer rather than the manufacturer.

Cover applies to matched indoor and outdoor pairs, not mixed kit

Refrigerant is treated as a consumable and is never covered

Annual servicing is a condition, not a suggestion. Skip it and the cover lapses

We register the warranty for you and send the certificate with the handover pack

We give two years on our own workmanship on top of whatever the manufacturer provides.

Common questions

What business customers ask first

Can you work around our opening hours?

Yes. Shops, restaurants and gyms are normally fitted in the evening or at the weekend so they never have to close. We do not charge a premium on the labour rate for it, and the programme in your quote says exactly which nights we need.

Do we legally need a TM44 inspection?

If the air conditioning in your building has an effective rated output over 12kW, yes. It has to be inspected by an accredited energy assessor at least every five years, with the first inspection within five years of the system going into service, and the report goes on the national register.

That threshold catches more businesses than people expect. Four 3.5kW cassettes on one floor already crosses it. The duty sits with whoever owns or controls the system rather than with the company that installed it, so it is worth knowing where you stand.

What are our F-Gas duties as a business?

You are the operator, so the record keeping and the leak checks are legally yours. The trigger is how much refrigerant the system holds, converted into tonnes of CO2 equivalent: nothing is required below 5 tonnes, then checks every 12 months to 50 tonnes, every 6 months to 500 tonnes, and every 3 months above that.

A small split system sits under the line. A VRF serving a floor plate usually sits over it. We work out where each of your systems falls, keep the log, and carry out the checks as part of a maintenance contract.

Is a VRF system worth it over separate split systems?

Past about eight indoor units it usually is. One pipe network instead of eight, far fewer condensers to find space for, better part load efficiency, and central control over the whole building. Heat recovery models can take waste heat from a server room and use it to warm a north facing office.

Below that, separate splits are cheaper to buy, simpler to fault find, and a failure only takes out one room rather than a floor. We will tell you which side of the line you are on rather than selling you the bigger system by default.

Can you cool a server or comms room?

Yes, and it is a different job to comfort cooling. The load runs at full tilt every hour of the year, humidity matters as much as temperature, and there is no tolerance for a warm weekend going unnoticed.

That normally means close control units rather than standard splits, two systems where one failing would be serious, and remote alarms so you hear about a fault before the kit does. Manufacturers recommend four service visits a year on these rooms rather than one or two.

How quickly can you attend a breakdown?

Maintenance contract customers come first, with same day phone support and attendance the next working day as standard. Without a contract we fit you in around contracted work, which in summer can mean a wait. Parts for the major brands are carried on the van, so most faults are sorted on the first visit either way.

Can we reclaim the VAT and claim the cost against tax?

Commercial installations are standard rated, so a VAT registered business normally reclaims the VAT in the usual way. The zero rate that applies to homes does not apply to commercial premises.

The equipment itself is generally plant and machinery, which often means the Annual Investment Allowance can cover it against profits in the year you buy it. Replacing failing plant can be treated as a repair instead, which works differently again. We give you a clear invoice and your accountant decides the treatment.

What paperwork do we get at handover?

Commissioning sheets for every unit, the F-Gas record with the charge and the CO2 equivalent worked out, electrical certificates for the work we did, operating and maintenance manuals, warranty registrations in your company name, and a drawing showing where the pipework runs. It is the pack your insurer, your landlord and your next assessor will ask for.

Why it matters

What a neglected system costs you

None of this is scaremongering. It is what we find on first visits to systems that have run untouched for three or four years.

Running cost

up to 25%more electricity

A clogged filter and a dirty outdoor coil force the compressor to run longer and harder for the same result. It is the cheapest efficiency you will ever buy back, and it shows up directly in your running costs .

Warranty

voidwithout annual servicing

Every manufacturer requires it. A compressor is the single most expensive part in the system, and cover for it disappears the moment the service history has a gap.

Air quality

mouldin the drain and tray

Condensate trays sit wet all summer. Left uncleaned they grow biofilm, block the drain, and push water back into the room through the indoor unit.

Compliance

The legal side, in plain English

Two sets of rules catch out business owners, and both put the duty on whoever operates the building rather than on the company that fitted the system. Commercial installation is covered separately.

F-Gas leak checks

Systems are measured by how much refrigerant they hold, converted into tonnes of CO2 equivalent. Once a system reaches 5 tonnes, the operator has to arrange leak checks by a qualified engineer and keep records.

| | System contains | Leak check

| Under 5 tonnes CO2e | No legal requirement

| 5 to 50 tonnes CO2e | At least every 12 months

| 50 to 500 tonnes CO2e | At least every 6 months

| 500 tonnes CO2e and over | At least every 3 months

Source: gov.uk, checking F gas equipment for leaks , checked September 2026.

With R32 that 5 tonne line sits at roughly 7.4kg of refrigerant. A home split holds one to two kilos, so no checks are due. A commercial VRF usually sits well over the line, and hermetically sealed units under 10 tonnes are exempt either way.

TM44 inspections

If you own or manage a building with air conditioning over 12kW of effective rated output, an accredited energy assessor has to inspect it at least every five years, with the first inspection within five years of the system going into service.

Four 3.5kW cassettes in an office already cross that threshold. The report goes on the national register and the duty sits with the building owner or the person controlling the system.

Source: gov.uk, air conditioning inspections for buildings , checked September 2026.

We flag systems over the threshold during servicing and track the renewal date so it never creeps up on you.

Common questions

Servicing, answered

What happens if I skip a service?

Two things. The system gets less efficient, because a blocked filter and a dirty coil make the compressor work harder for the same cooling, and you pay for that on the meter every month.

The bigger one is the warranty. Every manufacturer makes annual servicing a condition of their five to ten year cover. Miss it and a compressor failure in year four stops being their problem and starts being your bill.

What actually happens on a service visit?

Filters out and washed, indoor and outdoor coils cleaned, condensate tray and drain cleared and tested, refrigerant pressures and temperatures checked against the design figures, electrical connections checked for heat damage, fan bearings listened to, and the controls run through every mode. You get a written report with the readings, not just a tick.

Can you service a system somebody else installed?

Yes, and a lot of our service work is exactly that. The first visit takes a little longer because we record what is there, check it was installed properly and note anything that needs putting right. If we find something dangerous or badly done we tell you plainly, with photographs, and quote for the repair separately.

How often does a system need servicing?

Once a year for a home . Twice a year for most commercial systems , which is what the manufacturers specify in a working environment. Four times a year for server rooms, where the kit runs at full load every hour and nobody is in the room to notice a problem.

Do I have to take a contract?

No. One off services are £129 for a single unit, which is more than the plan price because we are fitting you in rather than routing you into a planned run. The plans exist because they are cheaper for you and easier for us to schedule, not to tie anybody in.

Repairs and callouts

What goes wrong

Six faults that account for most of our callouts

We attend breakdowns across the North West . Two of these you can check yourself in five minutes. We would rather tell you that than charge you to come out and press a button on a remote.

Blowing warm air
Check the mode first

Usually the remote sitting in heating or fan mode. If not, it is a dirty filter, a blocked outdoor coil, or refrigerant that has leaked away. A system low on gas will still blow, just not cold.

Typical fix
Clean, or leak test and repair before regassing

Water dripping inside
Nearly always the drain

The condensate tray blocks with dust and biofilm, fills, and overflows into the room. Occasionally it is a pump that has given up, or a drain run that was never laid to a fall.

Typical fix
Clear and flush the drain, replace the pump if fitted

Rattles, hums and squeals
Bearings and mounts

A squeal is usually a fan bearing. A rattle is often a loose panel or a bracket that has worked loose. A deep hum from outside can be a compressor mount that has perished.

Typical fix
Fan motor, anti vibration mounts, or a tightening job

Tripping the electrics
Stop using it

Water where it should not be, a failing compressor, or a damaged cable. Repeatedly resetting a breaker on an appliance that keeps tripping it is how small faults turn into fires.

Typical fix
Insulation test, then the component at fault

Error code on the display
Tell us the code

Every manufacturer uses its own codes and they narrow the job down enormously. Read it out when you ring and there is a good chance the right part is already on the van.

Typical fix
Depends entirely on the code, so tell us what it says

Ice on the pipework
Turn it off

Ice on the copper or the indoor coil means poor airflow or low refrigerant. Running it like that will kill the compressor, which is the one part you really do not want to replace.

Typical fix
Airflow restored, or leak found and repaired

04
We carry the common parts

Capacitors, fan motors, condensate pumps, control boards for the major brands, and gas. Most visits end with a working system rather than a quote and a wait.

05
We will tell you when to stop spending

If the repair is close to the cost of replacing, you get both numbers and an honest opinion about how much life is left in the rest of the system.

06
Leaks get found, not topped up

Refrigerant does not get used up. If it has gone, it leaked, and putting more in without finding the hole is both against the F-Gas regulations and a waste of your money.

Common questions

Before you ring us

My unit is blowing warm air. Is it broken?

Check the mode first. It is genuinely the most common callout we get, and it is usually a remote that has been nudged from cooling into heating or fan only. The snowflake symbol is cooling, the sun is heating.

If the mode is right and it is still warm, the likely causes are a blocked filter, a dirty outdoor coil, or low refrigerant from a leak. The first two you can look at yourself. The third needs an F-Gas engineer, because topping up a leaking system without finding the leak is both illegal and pointless.

Water is dripping from the indoor unit

Almost always a blocked condensate drain rather than a leak of anything expensive. The tray fills up, water finds the lowest point and comes out of the front of the unit. Turn it off so you are not making more water, put a towel down, and ring us. It is normally a same visit fix.

How much is a callout?

£95 for the first hour including travel, then £45 an hour after that. Parts are quoted before we fit them. Service plan customers pay no call out charge at all, and Plus and Commercial plans get seen before anyone without a contract.

Do you repair systems you did not install?

Yes, and most of our repair work is exactly that. Daikin, Mitsubishi Electric, Panasonic, Toshiba, Samsung, LG, Fujitsu, Hitachi and Midea are all familiar. If a system is beyond economic repair we will say so and show you the figures rather than replacing parts on something that is going to fail again.

The system is 12 years old. Repair or replace?

Depends on what has failed and what gas it uses. A fan motor or a control board on a ten year old unit is worth fixing. A failed compressor usually is not, because the part and the labour together get close to a new system .

The other factor is the refrigerant. Older systems running R22 cannot legally be topped up at all, and R410A is being phased down, which pushes the price of a regas up every year. A current R32 system will also use roughly a third less electricity, which changes the sums.

CoolIn / Air source heat pumps

Air source heat pumps

Air source heat pumps
you can have this month

Every air conditioning unit we fit is an air source heat pump. It takes heat out of the outside air and puts it in your room, at around four and a half units of warmth per unit of electricity, and it runs backwards in summer to cool. No grant application, no cylinder, no six month wait.

Book a free survey
Compare it to gas

4.5 units of heat per unit of power

0% VAT until March 2027

1 day to fit a single room

Air source heat pumps in short

An air to air heat pump is an air conditioning unit run in reverse: it moves heat from outside into a room rather than making heat by burning fuel. It heats and cools from the same box, costs roughly a quarter of what an air to water system costs to install, and does not qualify for the Boiler Upgrade Scheme because that scheme only covers air to water and ground source systems.

What it is
An air to air heat pump, the same hardware as air conditioning

Seasonal efficiency
SCOP around 4.5, so 4.5kWh of heat per 1kWh of electricity

Installed cost
From £1,850 for one room, zero rated for VAT until 31 March 2027

Grant eligible
No. The Boiler Upgrade Scheme covers air to water and ground source only

Hot water
No. It heats air, not water, so the cylinder or combi stays

Cooling
Yes, the same unit reverses in summer, which air to water cannot do

Air to air against air to water

Two technologies with the same name and different jobs

The heat pumps in the news are air to water. The ones we fit are air to air. Both pull heat out of the outside air using the same refrigeration cycle. What they do with it afterwards is where they part company.

Air to air compared with air to water heat pumps
| |   | Air to air (what we fit) | Air to water

| Delivers heat through | A fan coil in the room | Radiators or underfloor pipes

| Typical installed cost | £1,850 to £8,200 | £8,000 to £16,000

| VAT | 0% until 31 March 2027 | 0% until 31 March 2027

| Boiler Upgrade Scheme | Not eligible | Up to £7,500 through an MCS installer

| Hot water | No | Yes, with a cylinder

| Cooling in summer | Yes | No

| Seasonal efficiency | SCOP around 4.5 | SCOP around 3.0 to 3.5

| Time to install | One to three days | Three days to two weeks

| Disruption | One core hole per room | Often new radiators and pipework

| Best for | Rooms you use, cheap heat, summer comfort | Replacing a boiler entirely

If your goal is to take the gas boiler out, air to water is the honest answer and we will tell you so. If your goal is a house that is comfortable in February and July without a five figure bill, air to air does that today.

Is your home suited?

Where it works well, and where it does not

Works well

Rooms you actually spend time in, rather than the whole house at once, which is how most home systems are designed

Homes where the boiler currently heats nine rooms to warm two

Loft conversions and extensions the existing heating never reached

Home offices, where the running hours are long and the room is small

Conservatories and garden rooms, which need cooling as much as heating

Flats on electric only heating, where the saving against panel heaters is enormous

Think twice

If you need hot water from it, because it cannot provide any

If nobody will service it annually , because the warranty lapses without it

If you want the gas meter gone, which needs air to water

If every room needs heating, because the unit count gets expensive

If the building is uninsulated and draughty, where the heat leaves faster than any system replaces it

If the outdoor unit has nowhere to go that meets the noise limit

If you are chasing the £7,500 grant, which air to air cannot claim

We install air source heat pumps across the North West, including Manchester , Liverpool , Stockport , Bolton , Warrington and Chester . See every town we cover .

Common questions

Heat pumps, answered straight

What is the difference between an air to air and an air to water heat pump?

An air to air heat pump moves heat from outside into the air of a room through a fan coil, which is what an air conditioning unit does in heating mode. An air to water heat pump moves that heat into water instead, which then feeds radiators, underfloor heating and a hot water cylinder.

Air to air is cheaper, quicker to fit, works in a single room, and cools in summer. Air to water heats the whole house and gives you hot water, costs several times more, and cannot cool at all. They suit different problems.

Can I get the £7,500 Boiler Upgrade Scheme grant?

Not for air to air. The Boiler Upgrade Scheme covers air to water heat pumps, ground source heat pumps and biomass boilers, and the installation has to be carried out by an MCS certified installer. Air conditioning in heating mode is outside the scheme.

Source: gov.uk, Boiler Upgrade Scheme , checked September 2026.

What air to air does get is zero rated VAT until 31 March 2027, which takes 20% off the installed price and needs no application, no paperwork and no waiting list.

Will a heat pump work in a British winter?

Yes, but with less output as it gets colder. We compare it directly to gas central heating in this article . Manufacturers rate units down to around minus 15°C and they keep producing heat there, just more slowly and less efficiently than at 7°C.

In practice, below about 5°C outside you notice longer warm up times. For an air to air system heating one or two rooms, keeping your existing heating for the handful of genuinely cold weeks a year is the sensible approach rather than the failure it is sometimes painted as.

Does it replace my gas boiler?

Only if every room has an indoor unit and you have another source of hot water. For most houses an air to air system is a supplement: it heats the rooms you actually use, cheaply, for most of the year, and the boiler covers the rest and the taps. If you want to remove the boiler entirely, that is an air to water conversation and a much bigger job.

How efficient is it really?

A current wall unit has a SCOP of around 4.5, which means four and a half units of heat for every unit of electricity, averaged across a heating season rather than on a mild day. A gas boiler running at 88% gives you 0.88 units of heat per unit of gas. Because electricity costs roughly four times what gas does per kWh, the two land close on a like for like basis, and the heat pump wins clearly once you count not heating the rooms you are not in.

Do heat pumps need planning permission?

Usually not, and the rules are explained in full here . Since 29 May 2025 permitted development in England covers outdoor units up to 1.5 cubic metres, two units on a detached house and one elsewhere, with no minimum distance from the boundary, provided the MCS 020 noise standard of 42 dB(A) at the neighbour's window is met and the system is not used solely for cooling. Flats, conservation areas and listed buildings are more restricted.

Source: Planning Portal, air source heat pumps , checked September 2026.

CoolIn / Ventilation and air quality

Ventilation and air quality

Ventilation and air quality
because cooling only moves air around

Air conditioning recirculates what is already in the room. If the problem is stuffiness, cooking smells, condensation or thirty people in a studio, what you need is fresh air coming in and stale air going out. We design and fit both, usually at the same time.

Talk to us about ventilation
See commercial work

85% heat recovered by MVHR

Make up air for kitchen canopies

HEPA where it is genuinely needed

Ventilation in short

Ventilation and air conditioning solve different problems. Air conditioning changes the temperature of air already inside the building. Ventilation replaces that air with fresh air from outside. A room can be perfectly cool and still feel stale, because carbon dioxide, humidity and smells build up regardless of temperature.

Air conditioning does
Recirculate, cool, heat, dehumidify slightly, filter dust

Air conditioning does not
Bring in outside air, remove CO2, remove cooking smells

Heat recovery
MVHR recovers 85% to 90% of the heat from outgoing air

Kitchen extract
Needs matching make up air, or the canopy starves

Typical MVHR cost
From £5,200 for a commercial unit, installed

Damp and mould
Usually condensation, which continuous extract fixes at the cause

What we fit

Four ways to get the air moving

Heat recovery ventilation
MVHR

from £5,200installed

Continuous fresh air into the occupied rooms and continuous extract from the wet rooms, with a heat exchanger between them so you keep the warmth you have already paid for. Usually specified alongside a commercial cooling system rather than on its own.

Best for
Airtight new builds, deep retrofits, offices with sealed windows

Worth knowing
Needs duct routes planned early. Retrofitting into a finished building is possible but costs considerably more.

Kitchen extract and make up air
Canopies and supply

from £6,500installed

A canopy sized to the equipment underneath it, ducted to a fan that can actually shift the volume, and a tempered supply putting the same amount of air back so the kitchen is not running as a vacuum.

Best for
Restaurants, pubs, takeaways , staff canteens, dark kitchens

Worth knowing
Grease filters and duct cleaning are an insurance condition in most policies, not an optional extra.

Extract fans and systems
Wet rooms and workshops

from £450installed

Continuous low rate extract in bathrooms, utility rooms and salons, sized properly and ducted to outside rather than into a loft where the moisture just moves somewhere else.

Best for
Condensation and mould, salons, treatment rooms, workshops

Worth knowing
A fan that is too loud gets switched off, which is why the quiet ones are worth the extra.

Filtration and air handling
AHUs and fine filters

per project

Air handling units that filter, heat, cool and distribute in one plant item, plus finer filter grades where pollen, dust or clinical requirements mean the standard cassette is not enough.

Best for
Larger buildings, treatment rooms, gyms, manufacturing

Worth knowing
Finer filters restrict airflow, so the fan has to be specified for the filter, not the other way round.

We design and fit ventilation across the North West, including Manchester , Liverpool , Stockport , Bolton , Warrington and Chester . See every town we cover .

Common questions

Ventilation, answered

Does air conditioning bring in fresh air?

No, and this catches people out constantly. A standard split system recirculates the air already in the room, cooling it and filtering out dust as it passes. It removes no carbon dioxide, no cooking smells and no moisture from the building. If a room feels stuffy rather than warm, cooling it harder will not fix it. You need ventilation.

What is MVHR and is it worth it?

Mechanical ventilation with heat recovery. Stale air is extracted from the building and fresh air is drawn in, and the two streams pass either side of a heat exchanger so the outgoing air warms the incoming air without the two ever mixing. Recovery rates of 85% to 90% are normal.

It is worth it in an airtight building, where opening a window is the only alternative and throws away all the heat you have paid for. In a draughty Victorian terrace with gaps everywhere, extract fans usually make more sense for the money.

My commercial kitchen extract is too weak. Can you fix it?

Usually, and the cause is often not the fan. A canopy pulling air out of a sealed kitchen has to get replacement air from somewhere, and if there is no make up air supply the fan is fighting a vacuum. Doors get hard to open, the extract rate collapses and the room fills with heat.

The fix is a make up air system supplying tempered fresh air at the same rate the canopy removes it. We survey the canopy, measure the actual extract rate and size the supply to match.

Can ventilation help with damp and mould?

Often, because most domestic damp is condensation rather than water coming in. Moisture from cooking, showering and drying washing has to leave the building, and in a house with sealed windows and no working extract it lands on the coldest surface it can find. Continuous low rate extract in the wet rooms deals with the cause rather than wiping the symptom off the wall.

What filtration do you fit for allergies?

Indoor units on a home system take a washable pre filter as standard, which catches dust and hair but not pollen. Most manufacturers offer finer filter cassettes that fit the same units, and for treatment rooms or anywhere with a genuine clinical need we specify separate HEPA filtration rather than relying on what came in the box. Whatever is fitted needs cleaning on schedule or it becomes a restriction rather than a filter.

Why we started

Most complaints in this trade are not about the kit

The equipment from the major manufacturers is genuinely good. Daikin, Mitsubishi Electric, Panasonic and the rest all make units that will run for fifteen years if they are sized correctly, installed properly and cleaned once a year.

What goes wrong is everything around the equipment. A system sized on a rule of thumb that cannot cope in August. A quote that grows by six hundred pounds once the pipework is halfway up the wall. A condenser bolted under a neighbour's bedroom window. A company that answers the phone in June and does not in January, leaving you without a service plan or anyone to ring.

Every one of those is a process problem rather than an equipment problem, which means every one of them is avoidable. Getting the process right is the whole idea behind CoolIn.

01 We calculate rather than estimate
A room by room heat gain at survey, with the working shown on the quote. It takes longer than pointing at a wall and guessing, and it is the single biggest reason systems disappoint.

02 The price is agreed before we order
Fixed, itemised and valid for 60 days. If we measure something wrong, that is our problem to absorb rather than a line added to your invoice.

03 One company accountable
We survey it, specify it, install it and come back to service it. One contract and one number to ring, with no refrigerant circuit opened by anyone without current F-Gas certification.

04 We say the awkward bits out loud
Heat pumps blow cool air during a defrost cycle. Outdoor units drip in winter. Tall rooms heat slowly. You will read all of that on this site before you speak to us.

Local questions

Asked most often in Manchester

Can I put air conditioning in a Manchester city centre flat?

Usually, with two conditions. Your lease almost certainly requires the freeholder or managing agent to approve anything fixed to the outside of the building, and the permitted development limits for flats are tighter than for houses. Where a wall mounted condenser is not possible, a balcony position or a self contained unit with no outdoor part are the alternatives.

Do conservation areas in Manchester stop air conditioning?

They restrict where the outdoor unit can sit rather than banning it. In a conservation area the unit must not be nearer to a highway that bounds the property than the building is, which usually pushes it to a rear elevation or a lightwell. Listed buildings have no permitted development rights at all and need consent.

Local questions

Asked most often in Liverpool

Do coastal properties in Liverpool need special units?

On exposed waterfront and coastal sites, yes. Salt in the air attacks the aluminium fins on a standard outdoor coil, and a condenser that would last fifteen years inland can start failing in seven. Manufacturers offer coated coil versions of the same units for a modest premium, and we specify those as standard within about a mile of open water.

Can you work around restaurant opening hours in Liverpool?

Yes, and it is most of our hospitality work. Installations run overnight or between lunch and evening service, the area is sheeted and cleared before you open, and there is no premium on the labour rate for evening or weekend work.

Local questions

Asked most often in Stockport

Why does my loft conversion need a bigger unit than the floor area suggests?

Because a room in the roof gains heat from three directions rather than one. The roof surface above it is in direct sun for most of the day, the space has less thermal mass than a room lower down, and warm air from the rest of the house rises into it. We size loft rooms about 20% above the figure a simple floor area calculation gives, which is the difference between a room that holds temperature in August and one that does not.

Will the outdoor unit fit in a Stockport terrace yard?

Nearly always. A domestic condenser needs roughly 300mm of clear space behind it and a metre in front for airflow, and it can go on wall brackets rather than the floor if the yard is tight. The 2025 permitted development rules removed the old one metre boundary requirement, which opened up a lot of small yards that were previously awkward.

No permitted development rights at all, so listed building consent is needed before anything is fixed to the structure. We prepare the application with unit positions, noise data and photographs, and we have the conversation with the conservation officer before quoting.

Conservation area frontages

The unit must not sit nearer a bounding highway than the building does. In practice that means rear elevations, courtyards and screened positions, and it is worth checking early because it can change the whole design.

Period homes in the villages

Solid walls, single glazing in places, and rooms that were never designed to hold a temperature. Sizing has to account for a building fabric that loses heat much faster than a modern house.

Retail on the Rows

Awkward access, shared structures and tight fitting windows. Slim ducted units hidden above a false ceiling usually beat a wall unit visually and satisfy the landlord.

Local questions

Asked most often in Chester

Can I fit air conditioning to a listed building in Chester?

Often yes, but it needs listed building consent because permitted development rights do not apply. What usually gets approved is a condenser in a rear courtyard or a discreet position not visible from a public highway, with indoor units chosen to avoid drilling through historic fabric where possible. We put the application together and talk to the conservation officer before you commit to anything.

What are the rules in a Chester conservation area?

Permitted development still applies but with an extra restriction: the outdoor unit must not be nearer to any highway bounding the property than any part of the building. It also has to meet the MCS 020 noise standard of 42 dB(A) at the nearest neighbouring habitable room window, and it cannot be on a pitched roof.

Local questions

Do I need permission for air conditioning in the Bowdon conservation area?

Permitted development still applies, with an extra restriction: the outdoor unit must not sit nearer to a highway bounding the property than any part of the house. In practice that pushes it to a rear or side elevation, which is usually where you would want it anyway. What size unit does a glass extension need?

More than the floor area suggests. A 20m2 extension with bifolds and a roof lantern can need 5kW where the same 20m2 of ordinary bedroom would take 3.5kW. We size on the glazed area and its orientation, because on a south or west facing extension the glass is doing most of the heating, not the room.

What the buildings in Wilmslow tend to need

Wilmslow work tends to be whole house rather than single room, and the finish matters as much as the performance.

Whole house multi splits

Four or five bedrooms plus a study, all running from one or two outdoor units. Getting the condenser count down is usually the design priority, which means sizing carefully so the outdoor unit is not the limiting factor on a hot night.

Discreet installation

Slim ducted units above a landing ceiling, with only a linear grille visible, are common here. They cost more than a wall unit and they are the difference between a system you notice and one you do not.

Home offices and annexes

Converted garages, garden rooms and above garage offices are rarely on the main heating system and run cold in winter and hot in summer. A single unit fixes both ends of that, cheaply.

Pools, gyms and cinema rooms

High heat loads in sealed rooms. These need ventilation designed alongside the cooling, because recirculating the same air harder does nothing for humidity or air quality.

Local questions

Asked most often in Wilmslow

Can you install air conditioning without it being visible from the road?

Almost always. The indoor side can be slim ducted so only a grille shows, and the outdoor unit can go on a side or rear elevation, in a screened enclosure or behind planting, as long as it keeps clear airflow of roughly 300mm behind and a metre in front. Boxing a condenser in tightly to hide it is the one thing that genuinely hurts performance, so we design the screen rather than bolting one on afterwards.

Will one outdoor unit run five rooms?

It can, but the outdoor unit caps the total. Five 2.5kW indoor units on a 10kW condenser gives you 10kW shared between them when everything runs at once, not 12.5kW. In a house where all five rooms are occupied on the same hot evening that matters, so we size the condenser against how you actually use the house rather than the theoretical maximum.

Local questions

Asked most often in Warrington

Why does my new build overheat when it is so well insulated?

Because insulation works in both directions. A modern home is built airtight to keep heat in, so when sunlight comes through large south or west facing windows the heat that arrives has nowhere to go. There is no draught to carry it away and the fabric is too light to absorb much. It is common for a new build to run hotter in July than a draughty Victorian house of the same size.

Can you cool a warehouse or distribution unit?

Not the whole volume, economically. Cooling a high bay shed to a comfortable temperature costs more than most operations can justify. What works is spot cooling over the areas where people actually stand, packing benches, pick stations and offices, and destratification fans to push warm air back down in winter rather than letting it sit in the roof space.

What the buildings in Salford tend to need

Most Salford enquiries are apartments, and most apartments come with a freeholder, a managing agent and a lease that has something to say about the outside of the building.

Quays apartments

Floor to ceiling glazing facing water, with no shading and windows that open a few inches at most. These flats have no way of shedding heat, which is why they are among the most uncomfortable homes in the region by July.

Freeholder and management consent

Nearly every apartment job needs approval before anything is fixed outside. We prepare the request with unit positions, noise figures and photographs, which is the difference between an approval and a refusal.

Systems with no outdoor unit

Where a condenser genuinely cannot be fixed to the building, self contained units that vent through a small core hole are the fallback. They are less efficient and noisier than a split, and we will say so, but they work where nothing else is permitted.

MediaCity offices and studios

Edit suites and equipment rooms with steady year round heat loads, and open plan floors that need zoning. Out of hours fitting so broadcast and production are never interrupted.

Local questions

Asked most often in Salford

Can I get air conditioning in a Salford Quays apartment?

Usually, but the lease decides. Almost all of them require the freeholder or managing agent to consent to anything fixed to the exterior, and the permitted development limits for flats are tighter than for houses. Where a wall mounted condenser is refused, the options are a balcony position if the lease allows it, a shared plant location agreed with the building manager, or a self contained unit with no outdoor part. We work out which applies at survey rather than after you have paid.

Why are apartments so much hotter than houses?

Three reasons stacked on top of each other. Large areas of glazing with no shading, windows restricted to a few inches for safety so there is almost no ventilation, and heat arriving from the flats around and below you rather than only from outside. A top floor flat with a west facing wall of glass can be twelve degrees above the outside temperature by evening.

Local knowledge

What the buildings in Oldham tend to need

Oldham sits between 150 and 300 metres above sea level in places. Winters run colder and longer than central Manchester, so we size and explain the heating performance carefully here.

Stone terraces and cottages

Thick gritstone walls hold temperature well once they reach it, which cuts both ways: slow to warm and slow to overheat. Core drilling takes considerably longer than through brick and we allow for that rather than discovering it on the day.

Pennine winters

At 250 metres you see more days below 5°C than in the city, and that is where an air source heat pump works hardest for the least return. We are straight about it: the system will still heat, it will just take longer on the coldest mornings and you will want a second heat source.

Mill conversions

Huge volumes, single glazed metal windows in some cases, and exposed brick with no insulation. Spot cooling in the occupied zones beats trying to condition the whole floor plate.

Saddleworth villages

Conservation areas across Uppermill, Delph and Dobcross, plus a fair number of listed cottages. Outdoor unit position is a planning question before it is a technical one.

Local questions

Asked most often in Oldham

Does a heat pump still work up on the Pennine edge in winter?

Yes, but with less output as the temperature drops. Manufacturers rate units down to around minus 15°C and they keep producing heat there, just more slowly and less efficiently than at 7°C. Above about 200 metres you get more days below 5°C than central Manchester, so we size for that and tell you plainly to keep your existing heating for the coldest stretch rather than pretending it will replace it.

Is drilling through stone a problem?

Not a problem, just slower and more expensive in time than brick. A gritstone wall can be 500mm thick and takes a proper wet core drill and patience. It is worth knowing because a quote that assumes a standard 250mm brick wall will not survive contact with a Saddleworth cottage, and that is where mid job price rises come from.

Free survey

What the buildings in Rochdale tend to need

Town centre retail

Littleborough and the moor edge

Exposed positions where wind driven rain hits the outdoor unit directly. Positioning and bracket choice matter more here than in a sheltered suburb.

Local questions

Asked most often in Rochdale

How often will filters need cleaning in a workshop?

Far more often than in an office. A domestic or office system is fine on an annual clean with one interim check. In a workshop, joinery unit or anywhere with airborne dust, filters can block within a couple of months, and a blocked filter costs you both efficiency and, eventually, the compressor. We set the service frequency to the environment and show you how to pull and rinse the filters yourself between visits.

Does leaving the shop door open make air conditioning pointless?

Not pointless, but it changes the design. An open door is a continuous cooling load that most sizing calculations ignore entirely. The answer is usually a combination of a correctly sized system and an air curtain over the entrance, which costs less than upsizing the cooling and works considerably better.

Local questions

Asked most often in Bury

Why does my loft conversion need more cooling than the room below?

It gains heat from three directions instead of one. The roof above it is in direct sun for most of the day, the structure is lighter than a room lower down so it has less thermal mass to absorb that heat, and warm air from the rest of the house rises into it. We size loft rooms roughly 20% above a plain floor area calculation, which is the difference between holding temperature on a hot day and not.

Can one outdoor unit serve the loft and two bedrooms?

Yes, that is exactly what a multi split is for, and it keeps one condenser on the wall instead of three. The thing to watch is that the outdoor unit caps the total output shared between the indoor units, so we size it for the case where all three rooms are calling at once on a hot evening, not for the average.

Local questions

Asked most often in Macclesfield

Can air conditioning go into a listed building in Macclesfield?

Often, but it needs listed building consent because permitted development rights do not apply at all. What tends to get approved is a condenser in a rear courtyard or another position not visible from a public highway, with indoor units chosen to avoid drilling through historic fabric where there is any alternative. We put the application together and have the conversation with the conservation officer before you commit to anything.

Is it worth having heating from it this side of the Peak District?

Yes, for most of the year. Between roughly 7°C and 15°C outside, which covers a large part of a Cheshire autumn and spring, an air to air heat pump heats a room far more cheaply than firing a boiler to warm the whole house. On the genuinely cold weeks it gives less, and above 200 metres you get more of those weeks. We are clear about where the line falls for your specific address.

Local questions

Asked most often in Wigan

My yard is tiny. Can the outdoor unit still go outside?

Almost certainly. A domestic condenser needs roughly 300mm of clear space behind it and about a metre in front for airflow, and it can be wall mounted on brackets rather than standing on the floor. Since 29 May 2025 there is no longer a minimum distance from the boundary for permitted development, which made a great many small terraced yards viable that previously were not.

Can you fit it if there is no rear access?

Usually yes. Pipework can run internally through a cupboard or riser and out at a higher level, or the condenser can go on a bracket above the yard. It adds to the pipe run and therefore the price, which is exactly the sort of thing we would rather establish at the free survey than halfway up a wall.

Local knowledge

What the buildings in Southport tend to need

Southport, Birkdale and Formby sit close enough to open water that corrosion protection should be part of every specification, not an upgrade.

Salt air corrosion

Airborne salt eats the aluminium fins on a standard outdoor coil. Within roughly a mile of open water we specify coated coil versions of the same units as standard. It is a modest premium and it adds years to the life of the condenser.

Victorian and Edwardian villas

Large, high ceilinged, often converted into flats. Where a building is in multiple occupation, a shared plant position agreed with the freeholder usually beats six separate condensers on one elevation.

Lord Street and the conservation area

The canopied frontages and the conservation designation limit what can go on a street elevation. Rear and courtyard positions, agreed in advance.

Hotels and guest houses

Room by room control matters more than raw capacity, and fitting has to work around occupancy. We programme these floor by floor, out of season where possible.

Local questions

Asked most often in Southport

Does living near the coast really affect the unit?

Yes, and it is the single most important specification decision in Southport. Salt in the air corrodes the aluminium fins of a standard outdoor coil, and a condenser that would run fifteen years in Manchester can start failing in seven within a mile of the sea. Every major manufacturer makes a coated coil version of the same unit for a modest premium. We fit those as standard on coastal addresses and we would rather explain why than quote cheaper and see it back in year eight.

Are you not a long way from Southport for a breakdown?

It is about an hour from us, which is the outer edge of our normal area. We are honest about what that means: service plan customers still get next working day attendance, but without a plan, in the middle of a July heatwave, you will wait longer than someone in Salford. If that matters to you, the service plan is doing real work rather than being an upsell.

What the buildings in Blackburn tend to need

Mill buildings in mixed use

Manufacturing and process

Climbing towards the moors, colder and more exposed, with the same honest conversation about heat pump output on the coldest weeks that we have in Saddleworth.

Local questions

Asked most often in Blackburn

Is air conditioning worth it in a Lancashire mill town?

The cooling matters for perhaps eight weeks a year. The heating matters for six months, and that is where these systems earn their keep here. Warming one or two rooms you actually use, at roughly a quarter of the cost of the same heat from an electric heater, makes more financial sense in Blackburn than the summer cooling does. The cooling is the part you will be grateful for in July.

Can you cool machinery rather than people?

Yes, and it is a different specification. Process and equipment cooling runs at a constant load year round, tolerates far less variation, and fails expensively. That normally means close control units rather than comfort cooling, a second system so one failure does not stop production, and remote alerting so you know before the machine does.

Where a property sits in a flood risk area, ground mounted condensers are raised on stands above the likely water level. It costs very little at installation and saves the unit.

Industrial and process plant

The chemical and manufacturing sites around Northwich need cooling that protects equipment. Different tolerances, different specification, usually duplicated systems.

Modern estates at Winsford

Newer, better insulated housing with the overheating profile that goes with it. Sized on glazing and orientation rather than floor area.

My property floods. Where does the outdoor unit go?

Off the ground. Local questions

Asked most often in Leigh

How do I know if my house is solid wall or cavity?

A rough guide is the age: built before about 1920 and it is probably solid wall, after about 1930 and it is probably cavity. The brick pattern helps too, because a solid wall usually shows some bricks laid end on. It matters because a solid wall loses and gains heat faster, so the same room needs more capacity than its floor area suggests. We check it properly at survey, since guessing wrong is how systems end up undersized.

Can you fit air conditioning in a takeaway?

Yes, and the cooling is usually the easy half. The harder part is the extract over the cooking line and the make up air that replaces what the canopy pulls out. Without that supply the kitchen runs as a vacuum, the extract rate collapses and the heat pushes forward into the counter area. We design the two together rather than treating the cooling as a separate job.

TITLE: Planning permission for air conditioning
DESCRIPTION: The permitted development rules changed on 29 May 2025 and now cover cooling as well as heating. What the limits are and what still needs consent.
================================================================================

CoolIn / Blog / Do you need planning permission for air conditioning?

Do you need planning permission for air conditioning?

12 September 2026 · By The CoolIn team, Air conditioning engineers, North West

For most houses in England, no. The rules changed on 29 May 2025 and they got considerably more generous, including for systems that cool as well as heat.

That last part matters. Before the change, permitted development covered air source heat pumps used for heating. Systems that also cooled sat in a grey area that made some councils awkward. They are now explicitly in scope.

What permitted development allows

For a house in England, an outdoor unit is permitted development if it meets all of these:

The unit is no more than 1.5 cubic metres , including its housing
Two units on a detached house, one on anything else
It meets the MCS 020 noise standard , which is 42 dB(A) measured at the nearest neighbouring habitable room window
It is not used solely for cooling , so a heat and cool system qualifies where a cooling only one does not
It is not on a pitched roof . On a flat roof it must sit at least a metre from the edge
It is not on a wall above ground floor level where that wall faces a highway

The old requirement to keep the unit a metre from the boundary has gone entirely. That single change made a great many small terraced yards viable that previously were not.

Where it does not apply

Listed buildings have no permitted development rights at all. Anything fixed to the structure needs listed building consent, and that is a real application with a real timescale rather than a formality.

Conservation areas keep permitted development but add a restriction: the outdoor unit must not sit nearer to a highway bounding the property than any part of the building. In practice that pushes it to a rear or side elevation, which is usually where you would want it anyway.

Flats are covered but with tighter limits, and your lease almost certainly requires the freeholder or managing agent to approve anything fixed to the outside of the building. That consent is a separate question from planning and it catches people out far more often than the planning rules do.

Scheduled monuments are out entirely.

The noise limit is the one people trip over

42 dB(A) sounds restrictive until you understand where it is measured: at the neighbour's window, not at the unit.

A typical domestic condenser produces somewhere in the high 40s to low 50s at one metre. Sound falls away with distance, and a fence or a wall between the unit and the boundary helps further. Most positions pass comfortably. A unit bolted to a party wall directly below a neighbour's bedroom window may not.

This is a calculation, not a guess, and it is part of a proper survey.

What we do about it

We check the designation of your property at survey, before quoting. That means looking at whether you are in a conservation area, whether the building is listed, and working the noise assessment for the position we are proposing.

If an application is needed, we prepare it. If a position will not pass, we tell you before you have paid for anything rather than after.

Source: Planning Portal, planning permission for air source heat pumps , checked September 2026.

One thing coming down the line

From 28 May 2026, MCS becomes the only certification scheme recognised for the planning standard. If you are reading this after that date and comparing quotes, it is worth asking which standard an installer is working to.

If you are weighing up whether the system is worth it in the first place, the running costs are the other half of the question.

Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland have their own rules and the limits above do not apply there.
