TITLE: Air conditioning running costs
DESCRIPTION: Real running costs for UK air conditioning, in pence per hour, with the sums shown. Cooling a bedroom, heating a room, and how it compares to a fan heater.
================================================================================

CoolIn / Blog / What does air conditioning actually cost to run?

What does air conditioning actually cost to run?

16 September 2026 · By The CoolIn team, Air conditioning engineers, North West

Everyone asks this second, right after the installed price. The honest answer is that it costs less than most people expect to cool a room, and considerably less than most people expect to heat one.

Here are the actual figures, with the arithmetic shown so you can put your own tariff in.

Cooling a bedroom

A 2.5kW wall unit is the standard size for a room up to about 15m². It does not draw 2.5kW of electricity. That number is how much heat it moves, not how much power it uses.

Once the room is down to temperature the unit throttles back and draws roughly 0.3kW. Working hard on a hot afternoon it might pull 0.65kW.

At 25p per unit of electricity:

| | Running state | Power drawn | Cost per hour
| Ticking over, holding temperature | 0.3 kW | 7p
| Working hard, pulling the room down | 0.65 kW | 16p

So a full night of cooling, eight hours with most of it spent ticking over, lands around 60p to 80p.

Heating the same room

This is where it gets more interesting, and where most of the value sits for a British climate.

Air conditioning in heating mode is an air to air heat pump. It moves heat from outside into the room rather than making it. A current unit has a seasonal efficiency of around 4.5, which means one unit of electricity delivers about four and a half units of heat.

That gives you heat at roughly 5.6p per kWh , against:

7.4p per kWh from a gas boiler running at 88% efficiency, with gas at 6.5p
25p per kWh from any plug in electric heater, because they are all exactly 100% efficient and no better

A fan heater and an oil filled radiator cost the same to run as each other. Neither can beat a heat pump, because they can only ever give you one unit of heat per unit of electricity.

The number that actually matters

The like for like comparison above understates it, because it assumes the boiler is only heating the one room you are sitting in.

In practice, firing the central heating to warm a home office means warming the hallway, the spare room and the kitchen at the same time. Heating one room with a heat pump while the rest of the house stays cold is a completely different bill.

There is a fuller treatment in air conditioning against a gas boiler . On our own gas boiler comparison you can put your room size and your tariffs in and see both numbers. On typical figures, heating one room for a six month season works out around £55 with air conditioning against roughly £291 if the boiler is warming the whole house to do it.

What changes these numbers

Your tariff. Everything above assumes 25p per kWh for electricity and 6.5p for gas. Both move, and the ratio between them is what matters, not the pennies.
How well the room holds heat. A solid wall Victorian room loses heat far faster than a modern insulated one, so the unit runs longer.
What size unit you have. An undersized system runs flat out and never gets there, which costs more than a correctly sized one that cycles.
Whether it has been serviced. A blocked filter and a dirty coil can add up to a quarter to the running cost. This is the cheapest efficiency you will ever buy back, and it is why annual servicing pays for itself.

The short version

Cooling costs pennies an hour. Heating one room costs less than any other electric option and usually beats running the whole central heating system to warm the same room.

If you want the figures for your specific rooms rather than a worked example, the survey is free and we will put the running costs in the quote.

TITLE: Should you heat with air conditioning instead of the gas boiler?
DESCRIPTION: An honest comparison of heating a room with an air to air heat pump against gas central heating, including where the boiler still wins and what the system cannot do.
================================================================================

CoolIn / Blog / Should you heat with air conditioning instead of the gas boiler?

Should you heat with air conditioning instead of the gas boiler?

8 September 2026 · By The CoolIn team, Air conditioning engineers, North West

Air conditioning heats as well as it cools, and for a lot of the year it heats more cheaply than a gas boiler. That is true, and it is also the part of the sales pitch that gets oversold.

Here is the version with the caveats left in.

Where it wins clearly

Heating one room rather than the house. This is the whole argument, and it is a strong one. If you work in a home office from nine until five, firing the central heating warms nine rooms to keep one comfortable. A single unit in that room, at around 5.6p per kWh of heat, is a fraction of the cost.

Against any electric heater. A fan heater, an oil filled radiator and a panel heater all deliver exactly one unit of heat per unit of electricity. A heat pump delivers about four and a half. If a room currently runs on electric heating, the saving is immediate and large.

Shoulder seasons. Through October, and again in March and April, outside temperatures sit in the range where a heat pump is at its most efficient. That is a big chunk of the heating year where it is simply the cheaper way to warm a room.

Where the boiler still wins

The coldest weeks. Output falls as the outside temperature drops, because there is less heat in the air to move. Below about 5°C you notice longer warm up times. It keeps working down to around minus 15°C, it just works harder for less.

Hot water. It cannot produce any. None. If you are hoping to remove the gas meter, that is an air to water heat pump conversation and a much bigger job.

Whole house heating. It only warms rooms with an indoor unit in them. Putting a unit in every room to replace a boiler gets expensive quickly, and at that point the sums usually favour air to water.

The things nobody mentions before you buy

It will blow cool air at you occasionally. Frost builds on the outdoor coil in cold damp weather. Every so often the system reverses for a few minutes to melt it, and the indoor unit goes cool while that happens. It is the defrost cycle, it is normal, and there is no way to switch it off.

The outdoor unit drips in winter. Melted frost has to go somewhere. We fit a drain and run it to a suitable outlet, but in a hard frost that drain can freeze and water can spill onto the ground below. Worth deciding at survey whether that matters where your unit is going.

Heat rises, so tall rooms are slow. In a vaulted lounge the warm air collects above your head while the floor stays cool. That is physics rather than the equipment, and destratification fans are the answer.

So what should you actually do

For most houses the honest answer is not either/or. Keep the boiler. Put air conditioning in the two or three rooms you actually spend time in. Use it for heating from September through to the cold snap and again in spring, use the boiler when it is genuinely freezing, and get cooling in July as the part you did not have before.

That is the combination that works, and it is what we fit most often.

If you want to see the numbers for your own room and your own tariff, the gas boiler comparison does the sums as you type. And if you would rather have the figures for your actual property, the survey is free.

TITLE: Why Should You Install Air Conditioning in Manchester During Winter?
DESCRIPTION: Discover the benefits of installing domestic air conditioning in winter, including shorter waits, better availability, and efficient heating for your Manchester home.
================================================================================

CoolIn / Blog / Why Should You Install Air Conditioning in Manchester During Winter?

Why Should You Install Air Conditioning in Manchester During Winter?

20 September 2026 · By The CoolIn team, Air conditioning engineers, North West

Installing air conditioning systems in winter offers significant benefits, primarily due to reduced demand, shorter installation times, and the ability to utilise units for efficient heating, ensuring readiness for summer. This proactive approach avoids peak-season delays and ensures year-round comfort for domestic properties.

As providers of domestic air conditioning solutions across the North West, including Manchester and Liverpool, CoolIn offers premium air conditioning systems and expert installation services for homeowners seeking year-round climate control. Find out more at Cool-in.co.uk.

Definition: Domestic air conditioning refers to climate control systems designed for residential properties, providing both cooling and heating functions to maintain comfortable indoor temperatures.

Why Consider Winter for Air Conditioning Installation?

Homeowners often associate air conditioning with hot summer days, but winter provides an opportune window for installation. Choosing winter offers multiple strategic advantages, ensuring a smoother, more cost-effective process.

How Does Winter Installation Address Supply and Demand?

The demand for air conditioning installation surges dramatically during warmer months, leading to stretched resources and longer waits. Planning ahead in winter allows you to bypass this peak-season crunch.

Shorter Lead Times: During summer heatwaves, installers' diaries fill quickly. Lead times for air conditioning installation can extend to weeks or even months. In contrast, winter offers greater flexibility and quicker scheduling.

Better Availability of Units: Exceptional summer heat often causes widespread shortages of air conditioning units. Major retailers have reported limited or no stock during peak demand. Installing in winter means better access to your preferred models and brands.

More Flexible Scheduling: Installers have increased availability in the quieter winter months. This allows homeowners in Manchester and the wider North West to choose installation dates that best suit their schedules, reducing disruption to daily life.

Reduced Installation Pressure: With less urgent demand, engineers can dedicate more time to system design, precise placement, and thorough testing. This leads to a higher quality installation.

Do Modern Air Conditioning Units Offer Heating Benefits in Winter?

Modern domestic air conditioning units are highly efficient heat pumps. This means they provide effective heating as well as cooling, making them a valuable year-round investment for your home.

Dual Functionality: Contemporary air conditioning systems are designed with heat pump technology. This enables them to warm your home efficiently during colder months. The same unit that cools your home in July can provide warmth in January.

Energy Efficiency: Air-to-air heat pumps are significantly more energy-efficient for heating than traditional electric heaters. For every 1 kilowatt (kW) of electricity consumed, a modern inverter air conditioner can deliver 3 to 5 kW of heating output [Source: Energy Saving Trust, 'Comparing Heating Costs' (latest edition)]. This can translate to substantial savings on running costs.

Some systems offer up to 65% lower costs compared to electric heaters, depending on insulation levels, outdoor temperatures, and usage patterns.

They can also provide around 30% savings compared to gas boilers under optimal conditions and specific energy tariffs [Source: Energy Saving Trust, 'Comparing Heating Costs' (latest edition)].

Improved Air Quality and Humidity Control: Beyond temperature regulation, these systems often include advanced filtration. This cleans the air of dust, allergens, and pollutants. They also control indoor humidity, preventing issues like condensation and mould, which can be common in UK winters.

Instant Comfort: Unlike radiators that take time to warm up, inverter air conditioners can reach target temperatures within minutes. They distribute warm air evenly throughout the room.

What Are the Typical Installation Timelines?

The installation process for domestic air conditioning is generally quicker than many homeowners expect, especially outside the peak season.

Single-Split Systems: For a single indoor unit and one outdoor unit, installation typically takes 4-8 hours, often completed within one day.

Multi-Split Systems: Systems with multiple indoor units connected to a single outdoor condenser usually require 1-3 days. This depends on the number of units and the complexity of pipe runs.

Ducted Systems: More extensive ducted systems for whole-house climate control can take 3-5 days or even a week. These often integrate with renovation work.

An experienced installation team like CoolIn ensures a clean, efficient process, minimising disruption to your home. Once installed and commissioned, your new system is ready for immediate use in both heating and cooling modes.

How is Domestic Air Conditioning Demand Evolving in the UK?

Domestic air conditioning is no longer considered a luxury in the UK but a practical necessity for year-round comfort. This shift is driven by several factors:

Rising Demand: The UK's summers are becoming consistently hotter, with record-breaking temperatures and prolonged heatwaves increasing the need for cooling solutions. Checkatrade's Home Improvement Index has reported significant year-on-year increases in air conditioning installations in UK homes, noting a 63% rise during a recent period [Source: Checkatrade Home Improvement Index insights].

Low Adoption, High Potential: Fewer than 5% of UK homes currently have fixed air conditioning [Source: Energy Saving Trust, 'Heat Pumps in UK Homes' (latest report)]. This compares to much higher figures in other European countries and the US. This low adoption indicates significant growth potential as homeowners seek to improve comfort.

Government Push for Heat Pumps: The UK government is actively promoting heat pump technology, aiming for 600,000 heat pump installations per year by 2028 [Source: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero, 'Boiler Upgrade Scheme' documentation]. This policy drive underscores the efficiency and environmental benefits of these systems, which modern air conditioning units embody. The UK heat pump market is projected to nearly double from $3.66 billion in 2025 to $7.30 billion by 2030 [Source: Grand View Research, 'UK Heat Pump Market Analysis' (2023 report)].

By installing your domestic air conditioning in winter, you secure comfort for the next summer and invest in an energy-efficient heating solution that aligns with modern environmental and economic priorities.

Key Takeaways

Installing air conditioning in winter avoids the high demand and potential stock shortages of the summer months.

Winter installations typically offer shorter lead times and more flexible scheduling options for homeowners in Manchester and beyond.

Modern air conditioning units function as efficient heat pumps, providing cost-effective heating during colder periods.

A single-split air conditioning installation can often be completed within one day.

Domestic air conditioning is becoming increasingly essential in the UK due to rising summer temperatures and government energy initiatives.

Proactive winter installation ensures year-round comfort and readiness for future heatwaves and energy savings.
